paper.title: Regret Bounds for Restless Markov Bandits

unmapped: Each arm is an irreducible (aperiodic) Markov chain evolving independently of the learner's actions; learner observes the state of the pulled arm only
Regret is measured against the optimal policy knowing all transition matrices and mean rewards (POMDP-optimal policy), not the best arm
Learner knows the number of states of each arm and (for the first bound) the mixing times
settings.definition_quote: Given are $K$ arms, where underlying each arm $j$ there is an irreducible Markov chain with state space $S_j$ and transition matrix $P_j$. For each state $s$ in $S_j$ there are mean rewards $r_j(s)$, which we assume to be bounded in $[0,1]$. ... We are interested in competing with the optimal policy $\pi^*$ which knows the mean rewards and transition matrices, yet observes as the learner only the current state of the chosen arm.

unmapped: Arms are Markov chains evolving independently of actions; regret against optimal policy

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Average-reward reinforcement learning in a finite MDP with colored state-action pairs, not a bandit problem
unmapped: Learner knows coloring, translation functions and support bound B
settings.definition_quote: An $\veps$-structured MDP is an MDP with finite state space $S$, finite action space $A$, transition probability distributions $p(\cdot|s,a)$, mean rewards $r(s,a)\in[0,1]$, and a coloring function $c:S\times A \to \mathcal{C}$...

algorithms.name: Restless bandits algorithm (colored UCRL2 on the T-step representation)

symbols.Prod_4D: prod_{j=1}^K (4 D_j), D_j diameter of arm j's Markov chain

conditions: all arms are irreducible aperiodic Markov chains
learner knows number of states and mixing times of each arm

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Consider a restless bandit with $K$ aperiodic arms having state spaces~$S_j$, diameters $D_j$, and mixing times $\Tmix^j$ ($j=1,\ldots,K$). Then with probability at least $1-\delta$ the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:gen} ... after $T$ steps is upper bounded by ${\rm const} \cdot S \cdot \Tmix^{3/2} \cdot \prod_{j=1}^K(4D_j) \cdot \max_i \log (D_i) \cdot \log^{2} (T/\delta) \cdot \sqrt{T}$

results.notes: Unspecified constant, recorded as O. Regret = T rho* - sum r_t (random rewards). Paper says horizon can be removed via doubling trick with worse constants.

conditions: all arms are irreducible aperiodic Markov chains
tuning: run in rounds of length 2^i with confidence delta/2^i, guessing T_mix upper bound a(t) = log t

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Further, the dependence on $\Tmix$ can be eliminated to show that with probability at least $1-\delta$ the regret is bounded by ${O}\left(  S \cdot \prod_{j=1}^K(4D_j)\cdot \max_i \log (D_i) \cdot \log^{7/2} (T/\delta) \cdot \sqrt{T} \right)$.

results.notes: Mixing time need not be known; proof mentions an additive constant depending on T_mix. Horizon labelled known conservatively, though doubling scheme is used.

symbols.S_tot: total number of states, S = K m

conditions: each arm has m >= 1 states, S = K m

source.label: thm:lobo
source.quote: For any algorithm, any $K>1$ and any $m\geq 1$ there is a $K$-armed restless bandit problem with a total number of $S:=Km$ states, such that the regret after $T$ steps is lower bounded by $\Omega(\sqrt{ST})$.

results.notes: Regret type not stated precisely; proof reduces to the adversarial bandit lower bound of Auer et al. via deterministic cycles (made aperiodic).

symbols.B_supp: upper bound on support size of transition distributions in Psi_U
symbols.C_U: total number of colors for state-action pairs in Psi_U
symbols.eps_alg: structure parameter epsilon of the eps-structured MDP

conditions: learner knows coloring, translation functions and B

source.label: thm:aggsamples
source.quote: Then with probability at least $1-\delta$, after any $T$ steps colored \ucrl\ gives regret upper bounded by $42 D_\veps \sqrt{B C_U T \log(T/\delta)} + \veps (D_\veps+2) T$, where $C_{U}$ is the total number of colors for states in $\Psi_U$, and $D_\veps$ is the diameter of the aggregated $\veps$-structured MDP.

results.notes: MDP (RL) result, out of scope; regret relative to optimal average reward.
